p.x:
My mysterious vision condition keeps deteriorating

(I'll leave this here to spread awareness)

Some people are affected by an unknown condition where, several times through the day, they suddenly get a random blind spot in their vision. It is very noticeable when blinking, like a camera flash, usually lasts 5-10 minutes, and goes away. In some very rare cases, though, the spot stays, becoming a *permanent scotoma". 💀

This is not to be confused with floaters or migraine auras - these are actual blind spots, in a fixed position of one eye.

I've spent several days, and a lot of money, trying to figure this out, but tests all come clear, and doctors have no idea. Turns out this condition is undocumented. There is a Facebook Group of people who report very similar symptoms:

"Bright spots when blinking"

Despite being worrisome, the spots are too small to show up on imaging exams, and, through 10 years, I've barely accumulated 10 spots, so, it seems unlikely I'll ever go blind from this. Yet, it is certainly annoying, specially given that a bad luck could cause a permanent spot in the center, which would be somewhat disabling. It would be comforting to stop the disease from progressing.

We know that lowering the head or drinking a lot of water during a spot makes it go away faster, and we strongly suspect it is related to small vasoconstrictions in the retina. But, in general, this disease is poorly understood, and too niche/harmless to justify serious research, so, nobody knows what causes it, nor how to prevent the disease from progressing.

I wonder if, is the future, AIs will be able to figure it out?

p.x:
Thesis: 

TPOT functions as a spiritual expression of Trump-era neofascism: a postmodern political religion that sacralizes collapse and rebirth, aestheticizes politics through memes and irony, and binds insiders through a shared gnosis of transcendence against “normie” masses. Its refusal to engage with conventional politics mirrors fascism’s claim to be “beyond politics”: by treating ordinary politics as profane and unworthy, TPOT simultaneously validates the status quo and imagines a higher sacred order. In this way, vibes become liturgy, irony becomes theology, and disengagement itself becomes a spiritual-political stance.

p.x:
Claude Code cracked something open for us @every.

Now I ship to codebases I barely know, every feature we ship makes the next one easier, and non-technical members of the team use the terminal.

I’m genuinely grateful. So I brought its creators, Cat Wu (@_catwu) and Boris Cherny (@bcherny) from @AnthropicAI, on AI & I to say thank you—and to talk about everything they’ve learned from building Claude Code. We get into:

• The workflows Anthropic’s smartest engineers use to push Claude Code to its limits. Why they pit subagents against each other to get cleaner results, how they turn past code into leverage, and the slash commands and MCPs they rely on most.

• The product lessons behind one of the most loved AI agents in the world. How the team balances simplicity and power—building a tool that anyone can use, but that experts can bend to their will—and their philosophy of “unshipping,” or cutting back whenever there’s a simpler, more intuitive path to user intent.

• A peek into the future of coding with AI. The new form factors they’re experimenting with to make Claude Code more autonomous, more reliable, and more accessible to non-technical users

This is a must-watch for anyone—both technical and non-technical—who wants to learn how to use Claude Code like the people who built it.
